lede-coupling-locks.subject: mode-locking-at-small-integer-ratios
forms: Based on coupling between continuous oscillators, mode-locking at small-integer-ratio frequencies occurs.
Coupled continuous oscillators produce discrete mode-locked tongues; the integers count locked states, not pixels.
When two oscillators in a continuous medium couple, the locking spectrum is discrete even though the underlying motion stays smooth.

lede-discrete-features-inheritance.subject: universe-discrete-features
forms: The universe's discrete features (quantum numbers, three spatial dimensions, the gauge group) inherit from coupling between continuous parts, not from a separate quantization postulate.
Discreteness is what locking produces; it is not added to the substrate by hand.
Quantum numbers, dimensional structure, and gauge factorisation are downstream of coupling, not parallel posits.

mechanism-mediant-forced.subject: mediant-operation-uniqueness
forms: Based on energy conservation and stability under coupling, the mediant (a+c)/(b+d) is the only admissible binary operation between two locked frequencies.

Energy conservation forces the locked frequency between two bare frequencies; stability under coupling selects the smallest-denominator rational. Together these constraints have the mediant as their unique fixed point.
The mediant is not chosen; it is what remains when every alternative violates either the conservation or the stability constraint.

mechanism-stern-brocot-inheritance.subject: stern-brocot-tree
forms: The Stern-Brocot tree inherits its structure from iterated mediant insertion on adjacent fractions.
Iterating the mediant operation from 0/1 and 1/1 builds the Stern-Brocot tree depth by depth.
Stern-Brocot is the natural enumeration of the locked tongues the dynamics produces.

mechanism-forced-property.subject: framework-forced-quantities
forms: The framework's 'forced' property inherits from the no-alternative status of each constraint-satisfying step.
'Forced' is shorthand for 'every alternative violates a physical constraint'; the framework's quantities have no remaining degrees of freedom.
Each named structure in the framework is uniquely admitted by its constraints, not selected from a range of possibilities.

mechanism-integers-as-counts.subject: framework-integers
forms: The framework integers (13, 5, 1, 19, q₂, q₃) inherit their meaning as counts of mode-locked states, not as cell counts of a pixelated geometry.
Each framework integer answers 'how many tongues are locked at this depth?', not 'how many cells fit in this volume?'
The cosmic partition 13:5:1/19 is the substrate's spectral signature at Farey depth 7, not a cell count.

address-structural-invariance.subject: dimensionless-ratios
forms: Structural constants inherit their values from the combinatorial substrate and are invariant under any change of the physical medium.
The dimensionless ratios (Ω_Λ = 13/19, n_s ≈ 0.965, K_c = 2/π) are the same for any observer at any cosmic epoch, in any unit system.
A structural constant is a contrabass pitch: independent of the medium it sits in.

address-dimensionful-medium-dependence.subject: dimensionful-constants
forms: Address constants inherit their values from the particular medium the universe happens to instantiate.
H_0, ℏ, v_EW, the Planck mass tell us where on the structure we happen to be, not what the structure is.
An address constant is a tuba pitch: the same instrument in helium gives a different number.

forces-three-dimensions.subject: spatial-dimension-d-equals-3
forms: Spatial dimension d = 3 inherits from dim SL(2, ℝ) = 3 — the continuum closure of the Stern-Brocot symmetry group SL(2, ℤ).
Iterating the mediant generates SL(2, ℤ); the spatial manifold's dimension is fixed by the dimension of its continuum closure SL(2, ℝ).
Three-dimensional space is what the geometry must be to stay consistent with the substrate's combining operation.

forces-z6-mode-structure.subject: gauge-group-and-three-generations
forms: Three generations of fermions and the gauge factorisation SU(3) × SU(2) × U(1) inherit from Z_6 = Z_2 × Z_3.
The Klein bottle's two smallest accessible denominators (q₂ = 2, q₃ = 3) produce the Z_6 mode lattice; the Standard Model gauge group is its automorphism structure.
Three generations is what the framework gets for free once Z_6 is fixed.

forces-charge-quantization.subject: integer-charge-quantization
forms: Based on the mediant primitive identifying integer phase translations, S¹ compactness is forced; charge quantization in units of e/3 inherits from this.
S¹ has integer winding number for any continuous self-map; the framework's mediant primitive lands this on the charge sector.
Charge quantization is what integer winding number looks like once it acts on the gauge degrees of freedom.

residue-klein-bottle-topology.subject: admissible-field-mode-topology
forms: Based on substrate self-consistency, the Klein bottle is the only admissible field-mode topology.
The vacuum's topology is not a modelling choice; substrate self-consistency uniquely admits the Klein bottle.
Of all 2-manifolds, only the Klein bottle survives the substrate's parity-conservation requirement on field modes.

residue-four-mode-vacuum.subject: surviving-zero-point-mode-count
forms: Based on Klein-bottle topology and a Z₂ parity filter, exactly four zero-point modes survive.
A Z₂ parity filter on the Klein bottle admits four modes and no others; the vacuum has four constituent states.
Four is what zero-point counting gives when run on the substrate's actual topology, not on the assumed torus.

residue-Lambda-from-four-modes.subject: cosmological-constant-Lambda
forms: Λ ≈ 10⁻⁴⁷ GeV⁴ inherits from a four-mode vacuum, not from fine-tuning a many-mode sum.
The observed cosmological-constant value sits where four zero-point modes put it — no tuning required.
The 10¹²¹-order QFT discrepancy inherits from the torus-topology modelling choice, not from a physics mismatch.

predicts-omega-lambda-13-over-19.subject: dark-energy-fraction
forms: Ω_Λ = 13/19 inherits from Z_6 mode counting at Stern-Brocot depth 6: 13 locked-mode fractions, 6 unlocked modes (2 × 3), ratio 13 / (13 + 6).
The dark-energy fraction is 13/19 because that is the only ratio admitted by the substrate's mode counting at depth 6.
Ω_Λ = 13/19 = 0.6842, against Planck 2018's 0.685 ± 0.007 — a 0.07σ residual (parameter accounting per MANIFEST free_parameters_note).

predicts-n_s-golden-winding.subject: scalar-spectral-tilt
forms: n_s ≈ 0.965 inherits from Stern-Brocot self-similarity at the golden-ratio winding.
The scalar spectral tilt is what self-similarity gives at the 1/φ winding number; no inflaton potential is needed.
n_s ≈ 0.965 is the framework's only admitted value at the golden-ratio gap, matching Planck's 0.9649 ± 0.0042.

predicts-bare-K1-exclusion.subject: bare-K1-identities-status
forms: The bare K = 1 identities 8/35 and 27/8 inherit from substrate-scale arithmetic only and do not survive renormalization-group running to the electroweak scale; they are reference identities, not predictions.
8/35 and 27/8 land near the electroweak measurements but with the wrong sign of running; they are excluded from the corroborated list.
A bare K = 1 arithmetic identity is not a scale-consistent corroborated result the way a K < 1 substrate derivation is.

scope-why-these-parameters.source: README.md (What this framework does not do)
scope-why-these-parameters.subject: framework-question-class
forms: The framework's scope inherits from the question class the Standard Model is silent on: *why these Lagrangian parameters and not others*.
The framework speaks where the Standard Model is silent by convention; it does not displace the Standard Model on its home turf.
Standard Model cross-sections and decay rates are not addressed; substrate values of the Lagrangian parameters are.

scope-wightman-convention.source: README.md (What this framework does not do)
scope-wightman-convention.subject: standard-model-input-treatment
forms: Based on the Wightman-axiom convention that Lagrangian parameters are inputs to be measured rather than outputs to be derived, the Standard Model's silence on this class is structural, not an oversight.
The Standard Model treats parameters as inputs by research-program design; this framework treats them as outputs.
The Wightman convention is not under attack — it is just being moved one layer down.

comparison-program-class.subject: framework-comparison-class
forms: The framework's comparison class inherits from the program-level claim 'Standard Model parameters should not be free': GUTs, string theory, loop quantum gravity, asymptotic safety, causal set theory, the Wolfram hypergraph program, Geometric Unity.
This framework competes with unification programs that try to derive Standard Model parameters, not with the Standard Model itself.
Each member of the comparison class accepts the empirical burden of producing numbers the Standard Model only catalogs.

comparison-distinguishing-feature.subject: framework-distinguishing-feature
forms: The framework's distinguishing feature inside its comparison class inherits from its derivation depth: exact small-integer ratios at shallow combinatorial depth, not fits to free parameters in a high-dimensional manifold.
Predictions like Ω_Λ = 13/19 land at Stern-Brocot depth 6, not after Landau-pole running in a 14-dimensional manifold.
Shallowness is the framework's advantage: the predictions are reproducible without simulation.

anchors-K1-non-smooth-separation.subject: regime-separation
forms: Based on the K = 1 / K < 1 critical-line tongue-coverage discontinuity, the cosmological and particle-sector regimes are non-smoothly separated.
The Einstein (K = 1) and Schrödinger (K < 1) continuum limits are separated by a non-smooth tongue-coverage step.
There is no smooth path across K = 1; the two regimes cannot share an anchor.

anchors-two-minimum.subject: anchor-count
forms: The two-anchor minimum (H_0 and v_EW = 246 GeV) inherits from this regime obstruction; it is a structural feature, not a derivation gap.
Each regime requires its own anchor; reduction to one anchor is structurally obstructed.
Two is the minimum the framework can run on; not three, not one.

companion-stairs.subject: continued-fraction-staircase-at-depth-1-over-13
forms: Continued-fraction staircase at depth 1/13, budget 19. The configuration the headline Ω_Λ = 13/19 prediction lives in.
The framework's cosmic-partition number, made into a moving picture: thirteen locked modes against a budget of nineteen.
Each step of this staircase is a mediant insertion; depth 13 is where the Ω_Λ ratio closes.

companion-orbit.subject: stern-brocot-orbit-at-7-over-60
forms: A Stern-Brocot walk traced in polar coordinates. Eight lefts, one right, one left, three rights — the walk lands on 7/60 as a rational on the unit circle.
Modular orbit L⁸R¹L¹R³: a thirteen-step path through the Stern-Brocot tree ending at 7/60.
What the substrate looks like from inside the tree, as a single rational picks itself out of an unbounded enumeration.

companion-rose.subject: rational-rose-curve
forms: Rational rose curve. A Lissajous figure at a rational frequency ratio — the geometric counterpart to the staircase plateau at the same rational.
Two oscillators locked at a small-integer ratio, traced in phase space: a closed curve with as many petals as the ratio prescribes.
Every Stern-Brocot rational has a rose: the same dynamics, viewed as a shape instead of a frequency.

companion-spiral.subject: continuum-spiral-evolution
forms: Spiral evolution. The continuum-side companion to the discrete tree: the same substrate read at a different regime.
The K < 1 regime is not a sea of locked plateaus; it is a slow continuous wind, drawn here as a spiral.
Substrate dynamics outside the locked tongues, where the framework's Schrödinger limit lives.

companion-triangles.subject: farey-triangulation-of-upper-half-plane
forms: Farey triangles tiling the upper half plane under the SL(2, ℤ) action — the symmetry group that forces dim = 3 on the spatial manifold.
Every Farey triangle is a fundamental domain image; the tiling is what dim SL(2, ℝ) = 3 looks like before it closes.
The triangulation viewer for the same group whose continuum closure gives the spatial manifold its dimension.
